key_insight: Kiwi-Edit combines instruction-based and reference-guided video editing by generating high-fidelity training pairs at scale, enabling models to learn precise visual control beyond what language alone can specify.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between ambiguous natural-language editing instructions and the need for fine-grained visual control, overcoming the scarcity of high-quality paired reference training data.
method: Scalable data-generation pipeline that converts existing video-editing examples into high-fidelity instruction+reference training pairs.
Train a unified editing model conditioned on both textual instructions and visual reference guidance to produce temporally consistent, high-quality edits.
Mix and balance instruction-only and reference-augmented data to retain versatility while improving fine-grained visual accuracy.
impact: Enables more precise, controllable video edits in practical workflows without requiring large manually labeled paired datasets, benefiting researchers and engineers building multimodal editing tools.

paper_title: Kiwi-Edit: Versatile Video Editing via Instruction and Reference Guidance
paper_authors: Yiqi Lin, Guoqiang Liang, Ziyun Zeng, Zechen Bai, Yanzhe Chen
